explanation: The completion path assigns `s_axil_bvalid_next = s_axil_bready`, incorrectly making response validity depend on the master already being ready. In this test, `s_axil_bready` is held low until well after the register write completes, so the assignment leaves `s_axil_bvalid` low and the response handshake can never occur. Consequently `received` remains zero and the checker reports `response_timeout` at 570 ns.
evidence: Line 108 enters the completion path when `reg_wr_en_reg` is asserted because the testbench connects `reg_wr_ack` directly to `reg_wr_en`.
At completion, line 111 samples `s_axil_bready`, which is initially 0 and is deliberately asserted only later by tb.sv lines 69-70.
The same completion path clears the stored AW and W valid flags on lines 109-110, so the completed request cannot subsequently regenerate the missing response.
sim.log reports `sent=12 received=0`, showing register-side writes occurred but no AXI-Lite write responses were accepted, culminating in `response_timeout`.
